body_html:
Why Tampa homes are a termite magnet

Warm, wet, and built on sandy soil — Tampa is basically a termite resort. Subterranean termites are active here all twelve months, and a mature colony can chew through six inches of 2x4 in about five months. By the time you see mud tubes on the foundation or hollow-sounding baseboards, the colony has usually been working for a while.

How we treat it

We start with a full inspection (interior, exterior, crawlspace, and the soil line), then match the treatment to what we find:

  • Liquid barrier (Termidor-class): a treated zone around the foundation that termites can't detect and carry back to the colony.
  • Bait stations: in-ground stations for ongoing colony elimination and monitoring — ideal near slabs and landscaping.
  • Spot/wood treatment: targeted for localized drywood activity.

faq.q: How much does termite control cost in Tampa?
faq.a: Spot treatments run $300–$900, while whole-home liquid barriers or bait systems run $1,200–$2,500. Most quotes start with a free or low-cost inspection.

faq.q: How often should Tampa homes be inspected for termites?
faq.a: At least once a year. Tampa's climate keeps subterranean termites active year-round, so annual inspections (and continuous bait monitoring) catch colonies before they cause structural damage.
Yes — our liquid and bait programs include a re-treatment guarantee for the covered period if activity returns.
